subject.title: fix: prevent operational notices from leaking to source chats

question: When an operator-session redirect cannot be written, should OpenClaw expose the notice to the source chat, durably retry operator-only delivery, or intentionally discard it?
rationale: Failing open can re-expose the sensitive operational details this feature is meant to contain, while the current fail-closed implementation loses the only notice; repository behavior does not establish which security boundary maintainers intend.

options.title: Durable operator-only recovery
options.body: Keep the source suppressed only after a durable operator-owned queue or equivalent recovery path accepts the notice for retry.

options.title: Fail open to source
options.body: Return the notice to the source chat when redirect persistence fails, favoring immediate observability over confidentiality.

options.title: Accept log-only loss
options.body: Keep unconditional source suppression and rely on verbose logs when the operator transcript cannot be written.

recommendation.title: Durable operator-only recovery
recommendation.body: Keep the source suppressed only after a durable operator-owned queue or equivalent recovery path accepts the notice for retry.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans core reply delivery, heartbeat, global config, plugin hooks, and security policy, where this person has the strongest sampled implementation history.
